claims.text: DFT calculations can predict optimal dopants for reducing the sintering temperature of ceramic or powder materials.
DFT calculations can predict optimal surface modifications for reducing the sintering temperature of ceramic or powder materials.
DFT can be used to predict temperature-related material properties.
Applying DFT-predicted dopants or surface modifications can reduce the required sintering temperature.
The relevant starting material is in an unsintered or green state.
Dopants or surface modifications alter the material's potential-energy landscape.
Modification of the potential-energy landscape lowers the temperature required for sintering.
The untreated baseline requires a high sintering temperature.
DFT has limitations that can constrain prediction or screening.
There is uncertainty in predicting optimal dopants or surface modifications and their effects on sintering temperature.
Failure of the DFT-predicted dopants or surface modifications to lower sintering temperature would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The intervention is described as performing DFT calculations, but the experiment tests physical application of DFT-predicted dopants or surface modifications. A calculation alone cannot modify the material's energy landscape, so the physical intervention is inconsistently specified.
